Overall, the findings identify PEC as a potential competence pathway through which students may differ in their ability to convert LLM access into learning-related benefits, while structured prompt scaffolds may provide a scalable approach to reducing prompt-quality barriers in LLM-supported higher education.

item.title: Neuromorphic Computing in Human-System Interaction: A Scoping Review of Recent Developments, Key Challenges, and Future Research Opportunities
item.description:
International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction
This review examines recent advances in neuromorphic computing for human-system interaction (HSI). Inspired by the nervous system, neuromorphic computing utilizes spiking neural network models, event-driven processing, and biomimetic hardware to enable ultra-low power computing. The review analyzes 35 scientific papers published up to May 2026, classifying applications into five categories: brain-computer interface and healthcare applications, human-robot collaboration, neuromorphic synapse and hardware, affective computing and emotion recognition, and neuromorphic sensors and human-machine interfaces. Compared to conventional computing techniques, neuromorphic computing exhibits low-power consumption and faster processing. Recent advancements in neuromorphic computers include the development of memristors, flexible synaptic devices, and self-powered sensory systems. However, challenges such as standardization of datasets, system scalability, hardware-software integration, system explainability, data security, and data privacy can be recognized as the future research topics of neuromorphic computing for HSI. Overall, neuromorphic computing provides a potential HSI solution for a safer, more intelligent, and more human-centered future.

item.title: Beyond trustworthiness: Psychological and institutional drivers of university students' AI chatbot adoption in Vietnam
item.description:
Acta Psychologica
Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used in higher education, but it remains unclear whether factors associated with perceived trustworthiness are also associated with students' intentions to adopt them. Drawing on an extended UTAUT2 framework, this study examines how chatbot-specific attributes are associated with trustworthiness, performance expectancy, and hedonic motivation, and how these appraisals, together with UTAUT2 factors, relate to behavioral intention. Survey data from 604 university students in Vietnam were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that ethics (β = 0.294, p < .001) and design (β = 0.458, p < .001) were positively associated with perceived trustworthiness, while social influence was not. Design and interactivity were positively associated with performance expectancy and hedonic motivation. However, perceived trustworthiness (β = 0.043, p = .153), hedonic motivation, and effort expectancy were not significantly associated with behavioral intention. Instead, behavioral intention was most strongly associated with price value (β = 0.408, p < .001), performance expectancy (β = 0.281, p < .001), social influence, and facilitating conditions, and was strongly associated with students' self-reported continued-use tendency (β = 0.754, p < .001). Perceived trustworthiness was not independently associated with behavioral intention in the present model, whereas price value and performance expectancy showed the largest positive associations with intention. This pattern highlights the value of considering trustworthiness alongside instrumental, social, and institutional evaluations when explaining AI-chatbot adoption. The study extends UTAUT2 by integrating these adoption evaluations with an assurance-oriented appraisal of the AI system.

item.title: Exploratory Multimodal Machine Learning for Hazard Response Detection in Semi-Automated Rural Driving
item.description:
Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
Partially automated driving systems require drivers to remain cognitively engaged and prepared to respond to unexpected roadway hazards despite reduced direct vehicle control. In rural driving, low visibility and sudden animal crossings pose unique safety challenges to driver readiness and response capability. This study presents an exploratory multimodal machine learning framework for hazard-response classification under semi-automated rural driving. Using a high-fidelity driving simulator, EEG, eye activity, behavioral, and subjective workload data were acquired under manual and Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS)-supported conditions. Pre-hazard event-level features were evaluated using logistic regression, random forest, and multilayer perceptron classifiers with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Random Forest achieved the highest mean classification accuracy, although performance was constrained by class imbalance and limited sensitivity to brake events. Feature-importance analysis identified SART situation-awareness score as the most influential feature, followed by NASA-TLX workload, pupil-diameter change, and EEG-derived measures. These findings support multimodal hazard-response classification for future driver-readiness modeling.

item.title: Assessment of Static, Dynamic Visual and Multimodal Guidance to Support MI-BCI Paradigm Selection: A Human Factors Comparison
item.description:
Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
Sensory cue interface design critically affects the operational performance of motor imagery brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) in rehabilitation and human-machine interaction. Few studies have systematically compared visual and multisensory cues for MI control. This study investigated four cue schemes: static pictures, synchronized visual feedback, visual-audio combination, and visual-vibration combination, with evaluations focusing on BCI classification accuracy and user engagement. The results show that dynamic synchronized visual cues outperform static cues. Additional auditory and haptic stimuli cannot improve but interfere with stable MI performance. Pure synchronized visual cues achieve the most reliable MI control. This study provides ergonomic design guidelines for MI-BCI visual cue layouts.

item.title: Quantifying Shared Mental Models in Nursing Using Multimodal Physiological and Communication Data
item.description:
Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
Shared Mental Models (SMMs) are essential for effective nursing teamwork, yet existing assessments mainly rely on observations or self-reports that provide limited insight into team cognition during task execution. This study proposes a multimodal framework for quantifying SMM quality in virtual reality nursing simulations. Thirty nursing students (15 two-person teams) completed three collaborative clinical scenarios while electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking, and communication data were synchronously collected. Expert annotations were used to classify teams into high- and low-SMM groups. Results showed significant differences in neural activity, visual attention organization, and communication structures between the two groups. High-SMM teams demonstrated distinct EEG patterns, more organized gaze behaviors, and stronger connectivity between task-oriented communication components. These findings suggest that multimodal physiological and behavioral measures can provide objective indicators of SMM quality and support future development of real-time assessment tools for nursing teamwork and simulation-based education.

item.title: Ethical for Whom: A Systematic Literature Review of Multicultural Perspectives on Responsible AI Values for the Global Majority
item.description:
Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
Responsible AI principles like fairness, accountability, and transparency are built on Western institutional assumptions yet exported as universal standards. We systematically reviewed (N=41) studies from underrepresented regions to identify locally prioritized values and their tensions with dominant discourse. Three frictions emerged: epistemic (whose knowledge counts as ethical expertise), contextual (whether abstract principles survive local conditions), and infrastructural (how resource asymmetries constrain value realization). Our findings show Global Majority scholarship does not simply add new values to the list. They reconfigure ethics through lived experience by redefining the core logic: fairness shifts from individual parity to collective well-being; transparency shifts from technical disclosure to relational trust but bounded by protocol and custom; and accountability shifts from top-down audit to distributed responsibility shaped by labor conditions and data sovereignty. This study advocates for centering epistemic pluralism as a prerequisite for ethically legitimate AI governance rather than treating these frictions as implementation failures.
